messages.text:
Interesting wrinkle: the reference’s frequency ordering for equal counts is not stable across separate runs, which means some tied rows can legitimately trade places.

I’ll keep the deterministic ordering closest to the Rust tests, and I’m moving on to broader probes so we don’t overfit one unstable tie.

commands.commandLine:
"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command "@'
import subprocess, pathlib
root=pathlib.Path.cwd(); ref=pathlib.Path(root/'REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip(); td=root/'tmp_probe'
for i in range(5):
 r=subprocess.run([ref,'frequency','--limit','0','freq.csv'],cwd=td,capture_output=True)
 print(i, r.stdout)
'@ | python -"

"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command "@'
import subprocess, pathlib, sys
root=pathlib.Path.cwd(); ref=pathlib.Path(root/'REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip(); port=[sys.executable,str(root/'xsv_port.py')]
td=root/'tmp_probe'
more=[['fmt','--out-delimiter','h','in.csv'],['fmt','--crlf','in.csv'],['fmt','--ascii','in.csv'],['select','"'!h[]3[0]'"','sel.csv'],['select','h1[1]-h1[0]','sel.csv'],['search','"'^a'"','--invert-match','in.csv'],['search','"'^A'"','--ignore-case','in.csv'],['sort','-N','in.csv'],['slice','--index','1','in.csv'],['headers','--just-names','in.csv'],['frequency','--limit','1','freq.csv'],['frequency','--limit','1','--asc','--select','h2','freq.csv'],['stats','--median','freq.csv']]
for args in more:
 rr=subprocess.run([ref]+args,cwd=td,capture_output=True); pp=subprocess.run(port+args,cwd=td,capture_output=True)
 ok=(rr.returncode,rr.stdout,rr.stderr)==(pp.returncode,pp.stdout,pp.stderr)
 print(args, 'OK' if ok else 'BAD')
 if not ok:
  print('ref',rr.returncode,rr.stdout,rr.stderr); print('port',pp.returncode,pp.stdout,pp.stderr)
'@ | python -"
